faqs.q: What is the Grade 60 Stainless Steel Lifting Chain and where is it used?
faqs.a: The Grade 60 Stainless Steel Lifting Chain is a Grade 60 stainless lifting chain to Grade 60, dimensions similar to DIN 5687 for marine and corrosive sites where galvanized chain does not last. It is listed in sizes 3 mm to 26 mm, each size under its own Indus part number.

faqs.q: How do I read Grade 60 Stainless Steel Lifting Chain part numbers such as IH-LR-SC-G60-3MM?
faqs.a: IH-LR-SC-G60-3MM is the 3 mm size, 0.2 t WLL, IH-LR-SC-G60-10MM the 10 mm size, 2.45 t WLL and IH-LR-SC-G60-26MM the 26 mm size, 15 t WLL. The size table lists every Indus part number with its own dimensions and rating, so quote the full part number rather than the series name.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Grade 60 Stainless Steel Lifting Chain come in?
faqs.a: The Grade 60 Stainless Steel Lifting Chain is listed in 3 mm to 26 mm. Every size has its own Indus part number with dimensions in the size table; the [stainless steel chain shelf](/c/stainless-steel-chain) shows the rest of the range.

faqs.q: How should I pick the size of Grade 60 Stainless Steel Lifting Chain for my job?
faqs.a: Choose the chain size from the load and the rating in the Grade 60 Stainless Steel Lifting Chain table, then check the link dimensions (inside width, length and outside width) against the sprockets, hooks or fittings it runs on. Sizes run 3 mm to 26 mm.

faqs.q: What load rating does the Grade 60 Stainless Steel Lifting Chain carry?
faqs.a: The Grade 60 Stainless Steel Lifting Chain lists a working load limit of 0.2 to 15 t, set per size in the table in the unit the manufacturer rates it in. The working load limit is the most the part may carry in service; proof and breaking loads are test figures and never working limits.

faqs.q: What is the Grade 60 Stainless Steel Lifting Chain made from and how is it finished?
faqs.a: The Grade 60 Stainless Steel Lifting Chain is made from AISI 316L to 16 mm; AISI 318LN duplex from 16 mm and finished blasted. Stainless chain resists corrosion better than galvanized, and the listing gives the grade as 304 or 316 or AISI 316L where stated, so confirm the grade on your RFQ.

faqs.q: Does the Grade 60 Stainless Steel Lifting Chain come with a test certificate?
faqs.a: The Grade 60 Stainless Steel Lifting Chain is listed as Grade 60, dimensions similar to DIN 5687, and the manufacturer's test certificate comes with each consignment. For third-party certification or witnessed proof testing, say so on the RFQ.

faqs.q: Which parts connect to the Grade 60 Stainless Steel Lifting Chain?
faqs.a: The Grade 60 Stainless Steel Lifting Chain joins to fittings made for its link size, such as a hammerlock or connecting link from the same listing family, and other lifting chain is on the [alloy lifting chain](/c/alloy-lifting-chain) and [DIN link chain](/c/din-link-chain) shelves. [Our hammerlock versus clevis guide](/blog/hammerlock-vs-clevis-chain-fittings) compares the connectors.

faqs.q: How should the Grade 60 Stainless Steel Lifting Chain be fitted and inspected?
faqs.a: Inspect the Grade 60 Stainless Steel Lifting Chain for stretched, bent, worn or cracked links before use and remove damaged chain. Chain that carries a lifting load needs periodic inspection by a competent person; [our guide to proof load testing](/blog/proof-load-testing-lifting-gear) explains how rated chain is proof tested.

faqs.q: How does the Grade 60 Stainless Steel Lifting Chain compare with the Stainless Steel Lifting Chain?
faqs.a: The nearest sibling is the [Stainless Steel Lifting Chain](/p/stainless-steel-lifting-chain), and the two differ on pattern, material and finish. In detail, pattern is grade 60, dimensions similar to DIN 5687 here and not stated there; material is AISI 316L to 16 mm; AISI 318LN duplex from 16 mm here and type 304 or type 316 stainless steel there; finish is blasted here and polished there. Pick on the standard, material and finish your job calls for, then quote the part number from the size table.

faqs.a: The Stainless Steel Twist Link Chain is a stainless twist link chain for marine and corrosive sites where galvanized chain does not last. It is listed in sizes 5/64″ to 1/8″, each size under its own Indus part number.

faqs.q: How do I read Stainless Steel Twist Link Chain part numbers such as IH-LR-SC-SSTLC-008?
faqs.a: IH-LR-SC-SSTLC-008 is the 5/64″ size, IH-LR-SC-SSTLC-332764 the 3/32-7/64″ size and IH-LR-SC-SSTLC-012 the 1/8″ size. The size table lists every Indus part number with its own dimensions and rating, so quote the full part number rather than the series name.

faqs.q: Which sizes does the Stainless Steel Twist Link Chain come in?
faqs.a: Sizes on the Stainless Steel Twist Link Chain run 5/64″ to 1/8″. The size table gives each one its own Indus part number and dimensions, and the [stainless steel chain shelf](/c/stainless-steel-chain) lists the neighbouring products.

faqs.q: How should I pick the size of Stainless Steel Twist Link Chain for my job?
faqs.a: Start from the required rating, pick the size row in the Stainless Steel Twist Link Chain table, then confirm link dimensions against the fittings it must pass through. [Our guide to stainless steel lifting chain](/blog/stainless-steel-lifting-chain) covers sizing stainless lifting chain.

faqs.q: What load rating does the Stainless Steel Twist Link Chain carry?
faqs.a: The listing for the Stainless Steel Twist Link Chain gives dimensions and weights but no working load limit, so we do not quote one. If the chain is to carry a lifting load, tell us the load and application on the RFQ so we confirm a rated chain, such as the [alloy lifting chain](/c/alloy-lifting-chain) or a stainless chain that lists a working load limit; see [our guide to proof load testing](/blog/proof-load-testing-lifting-gear) for how rated loads are proved.

faqs.q: What is the Stainless Steel Twist Link Chain made from and how is it finished?
faqs.a: The Stainless Steel Twist Link Chain is made from type 304 or type 316 stainless steel and finished polished. Stainless chain resists corrosion better than galvanized, and the listing gives the grade as 304 or 316 or AISI 316L where stated, so confirm the grade on your RFQ.

faqs.q: Does the Stainless Steel Twist Link Chain come with a test certificate?
faqs.a: The listing for the Stainless Steel Twist Link Chain names neither a standard nor a certificate. If your site needs a test certificate, say so on the RFQ and we confirm what the maker can supply before you order.

faqs.q: Which parts connect to the Stainless Steel Twist Link Chain?
faqs.a: Connect the Stainless Steel Twist Link Chain with fittings matched to the link size: hammerlocks and split connecting links are the stainless options, and the [Grade 80 chain fittings](/c/grade-80-chain-fittings) are for alloy chain. See [our hammerlock versus clevis guide](/blog/hammerlock-vs-clevis-chain-fittings).

faqs.q: How do I install and check the Stainless Steel Twist Link Chain?
faqs.a: Check each link of the Stainless Steel Twist Link Chain for wear, stretch, nicks and corrosion, and take damaged chain out of service. Lifting chain should be inspected periodically by a competent person; see [our guide to stainless steel lifting chain](/blog/stainless-steel-lifting-chain).

faqs.q: How does the Stainless Steel Twist Link Chain compare with the Stainless Steel DIN 763 Long Link Chain?
faqs.a: The nearest sibling is the [Stainless Steel DIN 763 Long Link Chain](/p/stainless-steel-din-763-long-link-chain), and the two differ on pattern and size range. In detail, pattern is not stated here and DIN 763 there; size range is 5/64″ to 1/8″ here and 15 kg to 3750 kg there. Pick on the standard, material and finish your job calls for, then quote the part number from the size table.
